name: Plugin Tools Control
tag: One control panel for which AI agents can use which plugins and tools, with a log of every change.

scenarios.title: Audit who can use what
scenarios.ask: We have {plugins} plugins and {agents} agents. Find tools that agents can use but do not need.
steps: Inventory
Listed {=plugins * 4} tools across {plugins} plugins and mapped which of {agents} agents can call each one.
Usage reader
Checked 30 days of call logs. {=round(plugins * 4 * 0.45)} tools were never used by the agents allowed to call them.
Risk sorter
Marked {=max(1, round(plugins * 0.3))} unused tools that can write, send or delete as high priority.
Planner
Prepared a permission change for review: remove unused access, keep everything that was used.
followups: The plan only removes tools that were not called in 30 days. If an agent later needs one, it asks and you approve with one click.
Yes. The log shows who changed which permission, when and why, and you can roll back any change.
Monthly works for most teams, and the panel can run the audit on a schedule.

scenarios.title: Roll out a new plugin
scenarios.ask: Add a new {kind} plugin and give it only to the agents that need it.
steps: Installer
Added the {kind} plugin with {kind} tools in a disabled state.
Matcher
Suggested {=max(1, ceil(agents * 0.25))} agents whose jobs match the plugin.
Policy agent
Set read-only tools to allowed and anything that sends money, mail or deletes files to 'ask a person first'.
Tester
Ran each tool once in a sandbox and recorded the result.
followups: Can an agent request access later?
Yes. It sends a request with the reason, and an admin approves or declines it in the panel.
What does 'ask a person first' look like?
The agent pauses and posts the exact action, such as 'refund $40 to order 1182', and waits for approval.

scenarios.title: Stop a misbehaving tool fast
scenarios.ask: A tool is sending duplicate messages. It is used by {agents} agents and ran {calls} times in the last hour.
steps: Monitor
Spotted the call rate at about {=round(calls / 60, 1)} per minute, well above normal.
Kill switch
Disabled the tool for all {agents} agents in one action. The agents keep running without it.
Log reader
Found the cause: a retry setting changed in the last plugin update.
Planner
Prepared a rollback to the previous plugin version for your approval.
followups: Do agents crash when a tool is disabled?
No. They get a clear 'tool unavailable' message and either skip the step or hand off to a person, based on their settings.
Can we prevent this next time?
Yes. Set a rate limit per tool, and the panel blocks calls above it and alerts you.
